config.title: Validation & sanitisation

intro.title: Validation & sanitisation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Express server that validates and sanitizes user input from a form. You will learn how to use the express-validator library to check if data meets specific rules, like required fields or correct formats, and to clean it to prevent security issues. The core programming concept is input validation, which ensures your application handles data safely and correctly. You'll work with Express middleware, validation chains, and error handling to create a robust backend for processing user submissions.
intro.usecase: Validation and sanitization are essential security patterns in any web application that accepts user input. In real-world Express applications, this appears when processing registration forms, contact forms, payment details, or API endpoints that receive JSON payloads. For example, an e-commerce checkout form validates credit card formats and sanitizes address inputs to prevent SQL injection attacks. A user dashboard might validate profile update requests and sanitize bio text to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS). Without proper validation and sanitization, applications become vulnerable to data corruption, security breaches, and malicious attacks.

objectives: Apply validation middleware to an Express route to enforce input constraints.
Configure a schema-based validator to check request body data types and required fields.
Implement custom validation logic to handle specific business rules for user input.
Integrate sanitization functions to clean and normalize incoming data before processing.
Construct error handling middleware to return structured validation failure responses.
Manipulate request objects by stripping or escaping unsafe characters from user-provided strings.
Initialize and use a validation library to protect against common injection attacks in form submissions.

steps.title: Import Express and validation/sanitization libraries
steps.instruction: Import Express, express-validator for validation, and express-sanitizer for sanitization.
steps.hint: Use the 'require' statement to import each library. Express is the main framework, express-validator handles validation, and express-sanitizer handles sanitization.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express, express-validator, and express-sanitizer here
steps.expectedOutcome: The server file will have the necessary dependencies imported for building a validation and sanitization system.
successCriteria: Express, express-validator, and express-sanitizer are imported using require statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some libraries, but not all three. Make sure to import Express, express-validator, and express-sanitizer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Express, express-validator for validation, and express-sanitizer for sanitization using require statements.

steps.title: Initialize Express application
steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance and assign it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.hint: Call the imported express function without any arguments to create the app instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an Express app instance
const app = express();
steps.seedCode:
// Import Express, express-validator, and express-sanitizer here

// Create your Express app instance here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express application instance is created and stored in a constant named 'app'.
successCriteria: A constant named 'app' is declared and assigned the result of calling express().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the express() function to create the instance and assigning it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Express app instance wasn't created correctly. Remember to call express() and assign the result to a constant named 'app'.

steps.title: Configure middleware for JSON parsing
steps.instruction: Add the express.json() middleware to your Express app to parse incoming JSON request bodies.
steps.hint: Use app.use() to add the express.json() middleware. This should be added after creating the app instance but before defining any routes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding middleware to parse JSON
app.use(express.json());
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will now automatically parse JSON data from incoming requests, making it available in req.body.
successCriteria: The app.use(express.json()) middleware is correctly added to the Express application.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using app.use() with express.json() as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: add middleware using app.use() with express.json() to parse JSON request bodies.

steps.title: Configure sanitization middleware
steps.instruction: Add the express-sanitizer middleware to your Express app using app.use().
steps.hint: Use app.use() with expressSanitizer() to enable sanitization for all incoming requests.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding middleware to an Express app
app.use(expressSanitizer());
steps.expectedOutcome: The express-sanitizer middleware is configured and will sanitize all request data.
successCriteria: express-sanitizer middleware is added using app.use(expressSanitizer()).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using app.use() with expressSanitizer() as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sanitization middleware isn't properly configured. Remember to use app.use(expressSanitizer()) after your JSON middleware.

steps.title: Create a POST route for user registration
steps.instruction: Create a POST route at '/register' that accepts user data. Define it with app.post() and include a callback function that logs the request body.
steps.hint: Use app.post('/register', (req, res) => { ... }) and inside the callback, log req.body to the console.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route is defined at '/register' that logs incoming user registration data.
successCriteria: The route uses app.post('/register', callback) and logs req.body inside the callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.post() with '/register' and have a callback that logs req.body.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a POST route at '/register' with a callback function that logs the request body.

steps.title: Add validation rules to the route
steps.instruction: Add validation middleware to your POST route to check that the email, password, and username fields are present and correctly formatted.
steps.hint: Use the `body` function from express-validator to define validation rules for each field. Chain validation methods like `.exists()` and `.isEmail()`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The POST route now includes validation middleware that checks the email, password, and username fields.
successCriteria: The route includes validation middleware using `body()` for email, password, and username fields with appropriate validation methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some validation, but make sure to include checks for all three fields: email, password, and username.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation middleware is missing or incorrect. Use `body()` from express-validator to validate each field.

steps.title: Add sanitization to the route
steps.instruction: In the POST route handler, call req.sanitize() on the request body fields to sanitize user input before validation.
steps.hint: Use req.sanitize('fieldName') to escape HTML and remove script tags from each field in the request body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route handler now includes sanitization calls to clean user input before validation.
successCriteria: The POST route handler contains req.sanitize() calls for the relevant request body fields.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to call req.sanitize() for each field you want to sanitize.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax for using req.sanitize() inside the route handler. It should be called on request body fields.

steps.title: Create validation error handling
steps.instruction: Inside the POST route handler, add logic to check validation results using validationResult(req) and return a 400 response with error messages if validation fails.
steps.hint: Use validationResult(req) to get the validation errors. Check if errors are not empty with errors.isEmpty(). If there are errors, return res.status(400).json({ errors: errors.array() }).
steps.expectedOutcome: The route will now check for validation errors and return a structured error response when validation fails.
successCriteria: The route handler includes validationResult(req) to get errors, checks if errors.isEmpty() is false, and returns a 400 status with error messages in JSON format.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to: 1) Get validation errors with validationResult(req), 2) Check if errors.isEmpty() returns false, and 3) Return res.status(400).json({ errors: errors.array() }) when validation fails.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation error handling logic is missing or incorrect. You need to check validation results and return appropriate error responses when validation fails.

steps.title: Process sanitized data on success
steps.instruction: Inside the POST route, after the validation and sanitization, add logic to process the sanitized user data when validation passes. This should include extracting the sanitized values from req.body and sending a success response.
steps.hint: Use the validationResult function to check if there are no errors, then access the sanitized data from req.body and send a JSON response with a success message and the processed data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route will now handle successful validation by processing the sanitized user data and sending a structured success response.
successCriteria: The POST route includes logic that checks for no validation errors, extracts sanitized data from req.body, and sends a JSON success response with a message and user data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're checking if there are no validation errors, extracting the sanitized data from req.body, and sending a JSON response with a success message and user data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logic for processing sanitized data on success is missing or incorrect. Review the hint and analogous example to add the proper success handling after validation.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Make your Express server listen for incoming requests on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use the app.listen() method with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message when the server starts.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen on port 3000 and log a startup message.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a callback function that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly configured to listen. Use app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback.
